description.raw: Align the OpenProject-primary operating mode with RePlan sidecar data by validating how OpenProject tasks, statuses, dependencies, relations and time entries are represented in sanitized fixtures and how resource demands, capacities, AI-agent resources and quota constraints stay in RePlan without leaking private OpenProject pilot details.

elements.subject: Run OSS boundary checkpoint

description.raw: Check the public and private repository boundary, sanitized examples, documentation, license readiness and private-data leak risks without treating this as a public release launch. Produce blockers and non-blockers for later OSS readiness.

description.raw: Document how RePlan planned itself without private project data.

elements.subject: Improve generated static Gantt observability

description.raw: Document the static Gantt versus OpenProject plugin decision and make the generated Gantt page more readable for human validation.

elements.subject: Add Gantt resource allocation lanes

description.raw: Show resource allocation rows under each Gantt task and add an aggregated resource load section to the generated static dashboard.

elements.subject: Add operator project-state report

description.raw: Add a read-only report state command that summarizes sync health, planning health, tracking health, resource pressure and next actions for humans and AI CLI agents.

elements.subject: Add Plan vs Actual state tracking

description.raw: Extend the project-state report with task and resource-demand tracking rows for planned, actual, remaining, forecast and variance signals.

elements.subject: Add read-only tracking suggestion command

description.raw: Add an AI-CLI-friendly command that reviews Plan vs Actual signals and suggests safe operator follow-up actions without mutating canonical state.

elements.subject: Add tracking proposal candidate writes

description.raw: Extend tracking suggest with an explicit write-candidates mode that materializes supported tracking suggestions as reviewable proposal files without applying them.

elements.subject: Apply tracking remaining-work proposals

description.raw: Extend proposal accept so update_remaining_work candidates generated from tracking suggestions can update resource demand remaining work through the explicit proposal review loop.

elements.subject: Add tracking proposal loop observability

description.raw: Add report state and dashboard overview signals that show stale remaining rows, tracking proposal coverage and next operator commands.

description.raw: Render tracking proposal loop summary and rows in the generated static dashboard for human observability.

elements.subject: Prioritize tracking proposal loop rows

description.raw: Add status, priority, reason and deterministic sorting to tracking proposal loop rows for clearer human and AI operator decisions.

elements.subject: Plan MVP readiness audit

description.raw: Write an executable audit plan that lets two independent operators or AI CLI agents assess RePlan internal MVP readiness from the same evidence.

elements.subject: Plan post-MVP dogfood direction

description.raw: Document the post-MVP forks and approve the first short RePlan-on-RePlan dogfood cycle before adding new large features.

elements.subject: Run first self-dogfood tracking cleanup cycle

description.raw: Use RePlan reports to select the first real RePlan-on-RePlan maintenance action, clear stale remaining-work tracking proposals, fix the discovered audit id collision and record the resulting state.

elements.subject: Calibrate self-dogfood plan and resource model

description.raw: Review the RePlan self-dogfood roadmap, remove or defer invented work, agree the real near-term task sequence, calibrate resource classes and capacities, and define how subscription and limit-based AI resources such as Codex are planned and tracked.

elements.subject: Run full OpenProject-centered dogfood cycle

description.raw: Use OpenProject as the primary task source and RePlan as the resource layer for one complete working cycle: plan tasks, check resources, execute work, record actuals, analyze variance and make the next planning decision from the observed state.

elements.subject: Design OpenProject-native RePlan surface

description.raw: Decide how RePlan should become visible from an OpenProject-centered workflow, starting from links and adjacent dashboards and explicitly evaluating the path toward an OpenProject plugin or embedded panel.

elements.subject: Prototype OpenProject-native surface level 0 and 1

description.raw: Build the first practical OpenProject-native observability path for RePlan: stable OpenProject links, adjacent RePlan views and enough integration shape to decide whether a deeper OpenProject plugin is justified.

elements.subject: Reconcile dashboard daily load markers with weekly schedule semantics

description.raw: Make the dashboard representation of resource load explicit enough that daily visual markers do not mislead the human reader when the authoritative scheduling model is weekly or period-based.

elements.subject: Reconstruct OpenProject functionality and technical pitfalls

description.raw: Gather the OpenProject functionality, API behavior, operator friction and technical pitfalls already discovered during the RePlan pilot and self-dogfood work. The output must explain what OpenProject owns, which API behaviors caused errors or manual work, which actions are safe for AI CLI agents, and which operations require guarded helpers before the full OpenProject-centered dogfood cycle.

elements.subject: Evaluate OpenProject MCP, CLI and API options for AI CLI agents

description.raw: Compare the official OpenProject MCP server, the official OpenProject CLI, direct OpenProject API usage and RePlan-owned wrapper commands for the specific purpose of safe AI CLI agent work. The output must separate read-only access, write access, authentication, auditability, maturity risk and fit for the RePlan dogfood loop.

elements.subject: Design OpenProject AI CLI operating layer

description.raw: Design the narrow RePlan-owned operating layer that lets humans and AI CLI agents inspect and safely mutate the OpenProject-backed RePlan dogfood plan. The design must cover command boundaries, dry-run defaults, explicit apply gates, lockVersion handling, private binding usage, drift checks, destructive-operation gates, audit evidence and what remains manual in the OpenProject web interface.

elements.subject: Implement OpenProject preflight operator helpers

description.raw: Implement the minimum guarded helper surface needed before refactoring the live OpenProject plan. The helper surface should inspect the live project, list mapped and unmapped work packages, preview safe updates, require explicit apply for writes, preserve private bindings, avoid delete and recreate behavior by default, and produce machine-readable output for AI CLI agents.

elements.subject: Refactor live RePlan self-dogfood OpenProject plan

description.raw: Use the guarded OpenProject preflight helpers to clean up the live replan-self OpenProject project without deleting and recreating existing work packages. The pass must classify current work packages, preserve task identity, update statuses, dates and relations only through reviewed dry-run/apply flows, and finish with OpenProject/RePlan drift aligned.

elements.subject: Audit OpenProject agent tools hands on

description.raw: Install or inspect the official OpenProject CLI, test the live OpenProject MCP endpoint where available, inspect representative third-party OpenProject MCP/API client code, inspect practical API patterns and compare the results with RePlan current guarded helper scripts before finalizing the OpenProject AI CLI operating-layer design.

elements.subject: Design OpenProject work-package operator toolkit

description.raw: Design the full safe OpenProject work-package manipulation toolkit that RePlan and AI CLI agents need before refactoring the live OpenProject plan. The design must cover reusable patterns from the official OpenProject CLI and representative MCP clients, read commands, write commands, dry-run and apply gates, lockVersion handling, form validation, allowed workflow transitions, comments, metadata updates, relation handling, private bindings, prompt-injection boundaries, error taxonomy and the implementation slice that must exist before live plan refactor.

elements.subject: Implement OpenProject work-package operator toolkit

description.raw: Implement the minimum safe OpenProject work-package operator toolkit approved by the design. The implementation must provide AI-CLI-friendly read operations and guarded write operations for common work-package manipulation without raw curl, browser automation or delete-and-recreate shortcuts.

elements.subject: Implement dashboard load profile rendering

description.raw: Update raw Gantt JSON and static dashboard rendering so task resource rows use participation-window length and intensity-height fill, while the resource summary uses authoritative weekly buckets with a visible one hundred percent capacity waterline and overload above that line.

elements.subject: Implement guarded OpenProject work-package create helper

description.raw: Extend the OpenProject work-package operator toolkit with a safe create command so AI CLI agents can create new OpenProject work packages through a reviewed dry-run/apply gate instead of falling back to raw API calls, browser work or unsynchronized RePlan-only backlog notes.

elements.subject: Implement guarded OpenProject private binding helper

description.raw: Extend the OpenProject work-package operator toolkit with a safe private binding command so AI CLI agents can connect an existing RePlan task to a live OpenProject work package after guarded creation without manually editing ignored private binding files.

elements.subject: Add safe OpenProject dotenv loader

description.raw: Add a safe local dotenv loader for OpenProject operator scripts so live OpenProject credentials and target settings can survive agent session restarts without committing secrets or executing arbitrary shell code from dotenv files.

elements.subject: Add OpenProject backlog reconcile helper

description.raw: Add a guarded OpenProject backlog reconcile command that compares RePlan tasks with the private binding layer and the current OpenProject work-package set, reports missing bindings, proposes safe bind-existing or create-work-package actions, and applies only reviewed private binding updates.

elements.subject: Add OpenProject tunnel header support

description.raw: Add safe Host and X-Forwarded-Proto override support for live OpenProject API access through a local SSH tunnel while keeping committed examples generic.

elements.subject: Design read-only OpenProject plugin feasibility

description.raw: Define the mandatory read-only OpenProject plugin path for RePlan after the Level 0 and Level 1 OpenProject-native surface prototype, and choose the overlay JSON contract as the next implementation step.

elements.subject: Define OpenProject overlay JSON contract

description.raw: Stabilize reports/latest/raw/openproject_overlay.json as the RePlan overlay contract for generated dashboard views and the planned read-only OpenProject plugin.

elements.subject: Scaffold OpenProject RePlan overlay plugin consumer

description.raw: Design and scaffold the smallest read-only OpenProject plugin consumer that renders the RePlan openproject_overlay.json artifact inside OpenProject without owning RePlan data or mutating OpenProject.

elements.subject: Design safe OpenProject RePlan plugin deployment path

description.raw: Inspect the current OpenProject deployment shape and document a safe runtime path for installing the read-only RePlan overlay plugin, including custom image strategy, overlay artifact delivery, preflight checks, first runtime test choice, restart sequence and rollback plan. This sample work package is public-safe and does not contain private VPS paths.

elements.subject: Verify RePlan OpenProject plugin in throwaway runtime

description.raw: Build the custom OpenProject image containing the read-only RePlan overlay plugin, run it in a disposable OpenProject runtime, mount a generated overlay artifact, verify boot behavior, plugin route behavior, missing-overlay behavior, logs and security boundaries, and document the exact result before any private live OpenProject installation.

elements.subject: Prepare private live OpenProject RePlan plugin installation

description.raw: Prepare the guarded private live OpenProject installation of the read-only RePlan overlay plugin after the throwaway runtime proof. The task must verify backup and rollback readiness, identify the exact OpenProject Rails services that need the custom image, prepare the private compose override and image tag, prepare the generated overlay artifact mount, verify role permissions and browser access requirements, run dry-run or read-only preflight checks, and produce an explicit operator apply plan before any live OpenProject restart or plugin installation.

elements.subject: Execute private live OpenProject RePlan plugin installation

description.raw: Execute the first guarded private live installation of the read-only RePlan overlay plugin in the dogfood OpenProject instance. This task must use the accepted preflight plan, publish the generated overlay artifact to the private mounted directory, apply the compose override with the prepared custom OpenProject image to all Rails services, restart during an explicit maintenance window, verify OpenProject health, verify the RePlan plugin page through the normal browser path, run drift checks, inspect logs, and keep the rollback path ready until acceptance.

elements.subject: Improve live OpenProject RePlan plugin resource view

description.raw: Review the first live read-only RePlan plugin page from the normal OpenProject project workflow and improve it from a plain table into the smallest useful resource-aware OpenProject view. The task should keep the plugin read-only, keep OpenProject as the human task and Gantt surface, render only the existing RePlan overlay contract or a reviewed extension of that contract, show task-linked resource demand and warning information in a way that is easier to understand than the initial table, and explicitly decide which richer timeline or Gantt-like signals belong in this first project-level plugin page versus a later work-package panel or Gantt overlay.

elements.subject: Design OpenProject work-package RePlan panel

description.raw: Design the next OpenProject-native RePlan surface after the project-level plugin view: a read-only work-package-level panel or section that lets a human open one OpenProject work package and see the linked RePlan task, planned resources, actual consumption, remaining resource demand, warnings, proposals, evidence and links to the fuller RePlan dashboard artifacts. The design must keep OpenProject as the task surface, keep RePlan as the resource-planning sidecar, reuse the existing overlay contract or explicitly define reviewed contract extensions, avoid native OpenProject Gantt coupling in this slice, and produce a clear implementation backlog item for the first panel prototype.

elements.subject: Audit and synchronize project documentation

description.raw: Audit the current RePlan project documentation after the live OpenProject plugin installation, project-level resource-aware plugin view and work-package panel design work. Update related roadmap, design, specification and index documents so they consistently describe the current OpenProject-primary and RePlan-resource-sidecar operating mode, the implemented plugin state, the active work-package panel design gate and the deferred native OpenProject Gantt path. Keep historical decisions visible, avoid private live OpenProject details, and record any remaining OpenProject synchronization need explicitly.

elements.subject: Implement OpenProject work-package RePlan panel prototype

description.raw: Implement the first read-only OpenProject work-package-level RePlan panel prototype using Placement A from the accepted design. Add a plugin route for one work package, presenter lookup by OpenProject work-package id, a per-work-package ERB view with resource rows, planned/actual/remaining amounts, warnings, proposal and evidence summaries, compact timeline bars, safe empty states, and links from the project-level RePlan plugin page. Keep the plugin as a renderer over RePlan overlay artifacts, do not mutate OpenProject or RePlan canonical data, and keep native OpenProject Gantt modification deferred.

elements.subject: Stabilize OpenProject live helper timeouts after plugin deployment

description.raw: Investigate and fix the operational friction observed during the live work-package panel deployment: OpenProject Rails boot can exceed the Docker health and autoheal window after image replacement, and the guarded OpenProject API helper timed out after route verification. Define a safe operator procedure or helper timeout behavior so future plugin deployments and OpenProject task-status synchronization do not require ad hoc manual diagnosis. Keep the fix public-safe and do not commit private endpoints, tokens or live identifiers.

elements.subject: Optimize OpenProject plugin image build layering

description.raw: Split the OpenProject RePlan plugin image build path into a heavy dependency base image and a fast code-only image layer. Keep the exact OpenProject 17.6.0 builder and slim image pair, preserve the existing full-build fallback, make the throwaway runtime check use the same build helper as live operations, and document when to rebuild the dependency base versus when to copy only plugin code. This reduces iteration time for ordinary Ruby, route, controller, presenter and ERB changes without weakening the production-like image path.

elements.subject: Sync latest RePlan backlog drift to live OpenProject

description.raw: Use the guarded OpenProject/RePlan operator helpers to bring the private live OpenProject project back in sync with the latest RePlan self-dogfood backlog changes. Create or bind the missing live work packages for the recent accepted RePlan tasks, apply the missing dependency relations only through reviewed dry-run/apply helpers, rerun drift checks, and leave any remaining divergence explicit as drift or openproject_sync_pending. Do not use raw API calls, direct database writes, browser delete-and-recreate shortcuts, or committed private live identifiers.

elements.subject: Re-enter and rebaseline OpenProject-centered dogfood cycle after pause

description.raw: Resume the RePlan self-dogfood project after the month-long pause by checking the current OpenProject/RePlan state, explicitly documenting stale plan dates, deciding whether the active full OpenProject-centered dogfood cycle continues, splits, closes or gets replanned, refreshing the resource view for the next work block, and producing the next operator decision from evidence rather than chat memory. If live OpenProject access is unavailable, keep the OpenProject sync state explicit as pending and do not pretend the live backlog is aligned.

elements.subject: Record OpenProject wiki API gap and design token-based wiki access

description.raw: Record the verified OpenProject 17.6.0 gap where an API-token participant can neither read nor write wiki page text, decide the resolution direction, and design a separate OpenProject plugin that extends API v3 with wiki page collection, text read, create and update through upstream services and standard wiki permissions. Produce the gap record, the design document and the backlog tasks with resource demands. Keep the affected private project, its pages and identifiers outside the public repository. Source: GitHub issue 1.

elements.subject: Check upstream OpenProject roadmap for wiki text in API v3

description.raw: Search the upstream OpenProject community tracker for an existing request covering wiki page text, collection and write routes in API v3, including the direction of the bundled wikis module. Support the existing request or file a new one. Re-check on the live instance whether the documents module API is available, because the upstream 17.6.0 source mounts a DocumentsAPI while the issue states that no documents API exists. Record the result in the wiki API gap document. This task informs the plugin lifetime; it does not block the plugin.

elements.subject: Implement OpenProject wiki API plugin

description.raw: Implement the separate openproject-wiki_api gem under integrations/openproject/plugins: project wiki page collection, extended wiki page representation with formattable text and lockVersion, create through WikiPages::CreateService and update through WikiPages::UpdateService, standard API v3 errors, no new permission and no accept_key_auth patch. Extend the plugin scaffold check to cover the new gem and generalize scripts/build-openproject-plugin-image.sh so the custom OpenProject image carries every plugin directory with one Gemfile.plugins entry per gem.

elements.subject: Verify OpenProject wiki API plugin in a throwaway runtime

description.raw: Build the custom OpenProject image with both the RePlan overlay plugin and the wiki API plugin, boot a disposable OpenProject runtime, and verify with an API token: list pages, read text, create, update, stale lockVersion conflict, read-only member rejection and journal authorship. Resolve the four design verification points on representer caching, route patching, conflict status and missing wiki behavior, and switch to the documented own-namespace fallback if in-place extension is fragile. Confirm the overlay plugin routes still work. Do not touch the private live OpenProject instance.

elements.subject: Deploy OpenProject wiki API plugin to live instance and accept

description.raw: Deploy the verified wiki API plugin image to the private live OpenProject instance in a maintenance window with backup and the documented rollback path, keeping the same exact-version image for all Rails services. Accept against the issue criterion: the agent with its own token lists wiki pages, reads full text, creates a page and edits an existing one; a human sees the agent edit in the browser and the agent sees a human edit through the API; no password and no HTML parsing. Record a sanitized result document and close GitHub issue 1. Moving the affected project's knowledge back into the wiki is that project's own task.

elements.subject: Restore green CI on main by removing the ripgrep dependency from the plugin scaffold check

description.raw: CI on main has failed on every push since 2026-08-07 because scripts/check-openproject-plugin-scaffold.sh calls rg, which the GitHub-hosted runner does not provide, so the MVP smoke stops before its first assertion. Local runs passed because rg is installed locally. Replace rg with portable grep -E and grep -F in the check, keep every existing assertion, confirm that go test and the MVP smoke pass on the runner, and record the seven-week red period as a calibration finding: local smoke is not CI evidence.

elements.subject: Fix actual audit id collisions and failed-command writes, add demand reopen and overrun acknowledgement

description.raw: Close GAP-015 and GAP-016, the two defects that surfaced in real self-dogfood use. actual commands must build collision-free audit ids, and a command that reports applied false must not leave any canonical or audit write behind. A consumed or closed demand must be reopenable through the CLI instead of by hand-editing YAML. A reviewed forecast overrun must be acknowledgeable so the tracking loop and the MVP smoke do not depend on an unresolvable suggestion. remaining_amount 0 must survive serialization. The same slice adds the scenario id to scenario apply audit ids. It starts by extracting one generic read-modify-write helper in the file store, because every writer method repeats that sequence and the atomicity fix must be made once, not per copy (GAP-019). Tests cover each case; no command default changes in this slice.

elements.subject: Close the post-pause audit hygiene debt in CLI usage, developer docs and the gap register

description.raw: Apply the confirmed low-risk findings of the 2026-09-21 project audit: add actual close-demand to the usage text, gofmt internal/app/workload.go, renumber the duplicated GAP-013, rebuild the implemented-command inventory and current block in docs/dev/getting-started.md from the binary, mark planned versus implemented surfaces and the reviewed write-back helpers in docs/spec/cli.md, record the duplicated OpenProject auth header construction and the response-body echo in helper errors as a known gap, and add a dated review addendum to the audit record covering the red CI it missed and the superseded dirty-tree finding. Changing mutation defaults to dry-run is explicitly out of scope.

elements.subject: Evaluate code-graph and semantic tooling for RePlan code quality analysis

description.raw: Decide whether graph- and semantics-based code analysis tools are worth using on the RePlan Go codebase for consistency, duplication, dead code, coupling and hotspot analysis. Use the tool survey of another code-analysis project as the candidate source, separate language-agnostic tools from Python-only ones, run a bounded trial of the shortlisted tools on RePlan, and record a decision document with findings, cost and a recommendation. Adopting a tool in CI is a separate follow-up task.

elements.subject: Select the next product slice from RePlan reports after the post-pause re-entry

description.raw: Prove the part of the full OpenProject-centered dogfood cycle that is still unproven: choosing the next work from RePlan outputs rather than from chat. Generate the state report, workload, tracking suggestions and the dashboard after re-entry, review them with the OpenProject Gantt and the RePlan panels, pick one product fork from the decision table of the post-MVP dogfood plan, and record the decision with the report snapshot it was based on.

elements.subject: Add a pinned Go and shell lint baseline to CI and gate new findings

description.raw: Introduce one pinned golangci-lint configuration with staticcheck, unused, gocyclo, gocognit, dupl and gofmt, run it once as a committed baseline report, and gate only findings introduced after the baseline in CI. Add shellcheck for scripts with the intentional CDPATH idiom excluded. Fix the small set of real findings the 2026-09-24 trial produced: the unused hasDependencyTriple, the staticcheck simplification, the gofmt drift and the few real shellcheck warnings; decide whether the test-only DryRun service wrappers stay. Existing complexity and duplication hotspots are reported, not refactored, in this task. Closes GAP-020 and GAP-021.

elements.subject: Move Python embedded in shell heredocs into tested script modules

description.raw: Move the 22 Python heredoc blocks, 3916 lines, from the OpenProject and planning shell scripts into modules under scripts/lib, leaving the shell scripts as thin entry points with unchanged names, flags, environment variables, dry-run defaults and the REPLAN_APPLY gate. Build the OpenProject auth header and parse HTTP errors in one place, and stop echoing raw response bodies into operator JSON. Add unit tests for the moved modules and keep the MVP smoke output byte-compatible. The live OpenProject helpers are not changed while the re-entry synchronization is in flight. Closes GAP-018.

elements.subject: Make the project-state report answer what the operator should do next

description.raw: Selected from RePlan reports on 2026-09-24 (docs/dev/next-product-slice-decision-2026-09-24.md). The state report defaulted to a July week at a September status date, listed only acknowledged overruns as next actions and missed every item waiting on a person. Make the default week follow the project status date; skip acknowledged overruns; list review-ready tasks, in-progress tasks whose only remaining demand is human, and tasks past their planned finish; rank next actions by who can act and by date; pin the state Markdown with a golden test before changing it (GAP-005).

elements.subject: Add page deletion to the OpenProject wiki API plugin

description.raw: GitHub issue 2, found during the live acceptance of the wiki API plugin by the affected project's agent. Pages can be created through the API but not deleted: DELETE /api/v3/wiki_pages/{id} returns 404 even for an admin token, so every page an agent creates can only be removed by a person in the browser or through a Rails runner. The acceptance skipped the create check for that reason. Add DELETE gated by the stock delete_wiki_pages permission, separate from edit_wiki_pages, with 204 on success, 403 without the permission and 404 for a missing or invisible page; document it next to POST. Prove it on the throwaway runtime, then deploy the same exact-version image to the live instance with backup and rollback, rerun the skipped create-then-delete check with a member token and close issue 2.

elements.subject: Clear the remaining amount when a demand is closed as consumed

description.raw: GAP-029. actual close-demand --status consumed kept the old remaining_amount, so a closed demand read as stale work and the MVP smoke failed through stale_remaining_count; the only fix was reopen-demand --remaining 0 and a second close, two audit records that say nothing new. Closing as consumed now sets an explicit zero in the same staged write and the same audit record, and says so in its output; closing as cancelled keeps the amount as the work that was not done. Unit test with a mutation check; close the demands of the state-report task with the fixed command.

elements.subject: Move the project status date through an audited command

description.raw: The project status date drives the default week of report state, replan next and tracking suggest, and marks which tasks are past their planned finish. It was moved by hand-editing .replan/project.yaml, without audit, so it lagged behind the real date (2026-09-24 on 2026-09-25). Add replan project set-status-date with --date YYYY-MM-DD or today in the project time zone, dry run, actor, reason and one audit record; change only the default_status_date field of project.yaml; warn when the date moves backwards. Move the dogfood project to the current date with it.

elements.subject: Warn when an accepted task keeps a planned window after the status date

description.raw: GAP-028. An accepted task kept its planned window long after it was done: in August one task kept a November finish, which pushed its successors into November once live relations were applied, and on 2026-09-25 two tasks needed a hand-written scenario to record their one-day execution. Add a validation and report warning for accepted tasks whose planned finish is after the project status date, and a next action for an agent to record the actual window through a scenario. Then clear the warnings on the dogfood project and push the dates to live OpenProject.

elements.subject: Remove dead code and align the workload spec with the binary

description.raw: GAP-021 and GAP-011. Remove hasDependencyTriple, which nothing calls, and the four actual dry-run wrappers that only tests call, moving those tests to the request flag the CLI uses. For replan workload, the spec lists filters the binary does not parse: implement --resource-class and --unit, make --week optional with the week of the project status date as default, as report state and next already do, and move --task, --include-scenarios, --from, --to and --status-date to an explicit not-implemented list so the spec promises nothing the binary ignores.

elements.subject: Pin the dashboard and Gantt HTML with golden files

description.raw: GAP-005 remainder. The dashboard and Gantt HTML writers are the largest code in the project and were checked only by a few marker strings, so a lost table, a broken column, a reordered list or bad escaping would pass go test and the smoke. Build a fixture overview that reaches every section both pages can render, including text that needs escaping, store the rendered index.html and gantt.html as golden files, and fail the test on any difference, with an update flag for intended changes. The state Markdown already has this protection since 2026-09-25.

elements.subject: Split the project-state Markdown writer into section writers

description.raw: GAP-020 hotspot. WriteProjectStateMarkdown in internal/reports/markdown.go is the second most complex function in the lint baseline (cyclomatic 79, cognitive 143). Split it into one writer per report section with no change in output, proven by the unchanged state Markdown and next-brief golden files, and drop its entries from the lint baseline. In the same slice close GAP-017, whose fix task was accepted and whose CI has been green on every push since, and refresh the GAP-020 measurement.

elements.subject: Honour capacity effective dates in workload and reports

description.raw: Found while planning RePlan with RePlan: the operator gave 5 hours a week from 2026-09-28 instead of the recorded 10, but workload, the dashboard and the Gantt load sum every capacity record of a resource and ignore effective_from and effective_to, so adding a second record would show 15. Count a capacity only for the days of the week it is in effect, use the capacity in effect on the project status date when no week is given, validate the date fields, keep TaskJuggler export honest with an explicit warning, and then record the operator capacity change as data.

elements.subject: Review the OpenProject RePlan plugin views on real work

description.raw: Resume the OpenProject plugin track where it stopped in August. The project-level RePlan page and the work-package RePlan panel have been live since 2026-08-15, but the re-entry questions whether they explain the resource layer and help on a real task were never answered by the operator. Walk through both views with the operator on current work, record what helps, what is missing or confusing and what a Gantt-like RePlan view inside the plugin must show, and decide the scope of that view.

elements.subject: Stop command writes from reformatting hand-maintained YAML

description.raw: GAP-022. Every command write unmarshals and marshals the whole canonical file, so one status change rewrites quoting, comments and key order of unrelated records and review diffs mix intended changes with noise. Change the file store to edit YAML nodes in place, the approach already used for the project status date, so a command changes only the records it targets. Prove it with byte-level tests on hand-written files and a real dogfood write.

elements.subject: Design the Gantt-like RePlan view inside the OpenProject plugin

description.raw: Step 3 of the accepted OpenProject-native sequencing: a controlled Gantt-like RePlan view inside the plugin, driven by openproject_overlay.json, that matches the OpenProject Gantt visual language without touching native Gantt internals. Use the operator review of the current plugin views as input, define what the view shows (task bars, resource load lanes, overload, actual windows, warnings), which overlay fields it needs, and how it is tested and deployed, and get the design accepted before building.

elements.subject: Split validateWorkspace into per-record validators

description.raw: GAP-020 hotspot. validateWorkspace in internal/app/validate.go is the most complex function in the project (cognitive complexity 168). Split it into one validator per record kind with no change in diagnostics, proven by golden diagnostics for both example projects and a fixture that triggers every diagnostic code, and remove its lint baseline entry.

elements.subject: Build the Gantt-like RePlan view in the OpenProject plugin

description.raw: Implement the accepted Gantt-like view design in the openproject-replan_overlay plugin, read-only over openproject_overlay.json, extend the overlay contract only where the design requires, cover it in the scaffold check and the throwaway runtime test, deploy it to the live OpenProject through the guarded image switch with rollback, and have the operator check it on real work.

elements.subject: Remove the four copied branches in import accept

description.raw: GAP-020 hotspot. ImportAcceptService.Accept (cognitive complexity 124) holds four near-identical 50-line branches, one per accept mode, reported by the dupl linter. Extract the shared flow, keep each mode difference explicit, keep command output and audit records byte-identical under the existing tests plus a golden run of every mode, and remove the baseline entries.

elements.subject: Make weekly workload honest for multi-week and concurrent demands

elements.subject: Review the consistency of the RePlan and OpenProject tooling for CLI AI agents

description.raw: Review how connected, uniform, understandable and DRY the agent-facing tooling is: the Go CLI, the scripts and their Python helpers, the agent kit and the process docs. Record the findings with evidence and a consolidation sequence; the operator picks which steps to run.

elements.subject: Give every OpenProject helper one JSON envelope

description.raw: Review finding C-08. Add one shared emit function in scripts/lib and a shell fail_json function, and move every helper and wrapper to them: ok, command, mode, counts, actions, warnings and errors as a list of code and message objects, never a bare error string; the drift check reports mode like the others; no plain-text failure on stderr. elements.subject: Make a helper exit non-zero whenever it reports ok false

description.raw: Review finding C-02. The OpenProject drift check, the resource schedule drift check and the status push report ok false yet exit 0, so set -e and && chains pass over a drift or a skipped transition. Derive the exit code from ok in the shared emit function, give drift its own documented code, and update the callers in scripts, the smoke and the agent kit that relied on exit 0. A test asserts the code for aligned, soft drift, hard drift and a skipped transition.

elements.subject: Fail an apply when the OpenProject token is missing

description.raw: Review finding C-01. Six helpers answer ok true, mode skipped and exit 0 when the token variable is empty, even with REPLAN_APPLY=1, so an agent takes nothing pushed for success. Under apply, a missing token becomes ok false with a non-zero exit; in a dry run it stays skipped and adds token_env_not_set to warning_codes, as the agent kit README already says. A test covers both modes for each of the six helpers.

elements.subject: Load the settings file in every agent kit script

description.raw: Review finding C-05. Source it in each of them, keep the allowlist that refuses REPLAN_APPLY and REPLAN_BIN from a file, and correct the README if any script is meant to stay without it.

elements.subject: Remove this repository's dogfood defaults from the agent kit scripts

description.raw: Review finding C-05. Fifteen scripts default the RePlan project to examples/replan-self, which the kit does not ship, and about ten default the OpenProject project id to replan-self, so a kit user who misses one setting works on another project of a shared instance. Without the setting, a script fails with missing_setting; this repository keeps its values in its own settings file. Bootstrap stops writing resource.human.maintainer into a kit user's bindings and takes the assignee resource from a setting. Smoke and the dogfood loop pass with the explicit settings.

elements.subject: Run the agent kit check with only the kit settings file

description.raw: Review finding C-05. check-agent-kit.sh passes every variable explicitly, which hides scripts that ignore .env.local or fall back to a dogfood default. elements.subject: Keep the existing private bindings when bootstrap runs again

description.raw: Review finding C-10. apply_openproject_bootstrap.py rewrites the private bindings file with an empty dependencies list and never checks whether it exists, which drops the relation bindings written by the relations helper. Merge into an existing file, keeping every binding it does not create, or refuse without an explicit flag. A test runs bootstrap over a bindings file that has task and dependency bindings.

elements.subject: Read and write the private bindings through one module

description.raw: Review finding C-04 and the surface map overlap of three bindings writers. Eight Python helpers re-implement the loop over the private bindings file. Add one module that loads it, maps tasks and work packages both ways, appends bindings and keeps unknown keys, and move the drift check, both pushes, the soft drift accept, the operator report, the relations helper, the overlay build and the toolkit to it. Bootstrap, toolkit bind and backlog reconcile write through the same function. Tests cover the module; the helpers' outputs stay identical on the dogfood project.

elements.subject: Keep the OpenProject status mapping in one place

description.raw: Review finding C-06 and the surface map overlap of status names. The mapping between RePlan tracking statuses and OpenProject statuses lives in the bootstrap plan, the status push, the toolkit and Go, and they disagree: the toolkit has no review_ready or cancelled and adds on_hold and done. Keep one mapping, used by every helper, let the toolkit's update-status take a RePlan status as well as an OpenProject name, and add a test that compares the mapping with Go's mapOpenProjectStatus.

elements.subject: Finish the shared OpenProject HTTP client and settings

description.raw: Review finding C-12. openproject_http.py is shared, but six modules redefine auth_headers and request_json and pagination is written three ways. Move request_json, one paginate function and a Settings.from_env reader into it, with the dotenv allowlist derived from the same list of settings, and remove the copies. Go reads the retries setting as well as the timeout. Tests cover pagination and settings; helper outputs stay identical.

elements.subject: Fix the relations pagination and the bootstrap page limit

description.raw: Review finding C-10. The relations helper starts at offset 1 and then adds the element count, but the OpenProject offset is a page number, so with more relations than one page it skips pages. Bootstrap reads one page of 500 work packages and matches subjects only there. Both use the shared paginate function; a test with a fake server serves three pages.

elements.subject: Retry only idempotent OpenProject requests

description.raw: Review finding C-09. The shared request function retries every method on a timeout or a 5xx, and the backlog convention recommends two retries, so a POST that timed out after the server created the work package can create a duplicate. Retry GET, and PATCH only with a lockVersion; for POST, report the failure with what is known and let the caller check before creating again. A test covers each method.

elements.subject: Report the actions already applied when a helper fails midway

elements.subject: Derive the self plan counts in the tests from the fixture

elements.subject: Count concurrent slots in the schedule drift check like the workload

description.raw: Review finding C-15, found while planning the review's tasks. check_resource_schedule_drift.py spreads every demand over its task days and sums the days of a week, so a concurrent slot used by five one-day tasks in a row counts as five of one, and the check reports the development environment overloaded in every week the Go workload shows at one of one. GAP-031 fixed this in Go only; the helper re-implements the workload. Make the helper take the weekly rows from replan workload instead of computing them, or, if a field it needs is missing there, add it to the Go command, so there is one workload calculation. A test plans consecutive one-day tasks on one slot and expects no overload.

elements.subject: Report the dates OpenProject moves when a relation is created

description.raw: Review finding C-16, found on 2026-10-15 while pushing this plan's relations. When apply-openproject-relations.sh creates a follows relation, OpenProject's automatic scheduling moves the successor to the earliest date the relation allows; nine work packages moved, and the helper still answered ok with only created_relation counts. An agent learns of it only if it runs the date drift check. The helper reads the dates of the affected work packages before and after, reports every moved date in its output with a warning code, and its operator next steps name the date push; the backlog convention and the kit README say to run the date drift after relations. A test with a fake server that reschedules the successor checks the report.

elements.subject: Edit a work package's subject and description through the toolkit

description.raw: Review finding C-17, found on 2026-10-15 while recording progress on a planned task. The toolkit creates work packages and updates status, dates, estimate, assignee, type and priority, but cannot change a subject or a description, so an agent that must correct one has no reviewed path and the rule against raw API mutation leaves it stuck. Add work-package update-text with --subject and --description, a dry run that shows the old and new text, REPLAN_APPLY=1, a lockVersion check that refuses when the work package changed meanwhile, and the RePlan task title kept in step, with a test against the fixture and the kit check.

elements.subject: Keep planned amounts and dates in a baseline and add replan baseline create

description.raw: Agreed with the operator on 2026-10-25 to see how far estimates miss. A baseline holds only task and demand refs today, so it does not keep the estimates: when a demand is split or re-estimated, the original amount is lost from the canonical files. Store each included demand's planned amount and unit and each included task's planned dates in the baseline, add replan baseline create (dry run by default, --write, an id, a name and an approving actor) that snapshots the current plan, and validate that a baseline never changes after it is written. Convert examples/replan-self/review/estimate-snapshot.2026-10-15.yaml, the original estimates of the tooling consolidation plan, into a baseline of this format.

elements.subject: Report estimate accuracy against a baseline per task and resource

description.raw: Agreed with the operator on 2026-10-25. Add replan report estimates --baseline <id>: for every task in the baseline, the baseline amount, the current planned amount, the actual consumption and the variance per demand, grouped by resource (the Codex CLI agent, the executor agent, the maintainer), plus schedule variance from the baseline dates and the actual finish. Demands added after the baseline, such as a Codex demand split from an agent demand, count toward the task they belong to and are listed as added. Markdown and JSON output; a test on a fixture with a split demand and a re-estimate.

elements.subject: Refresh the second project's agent kit after the release story

description.raw: Agreed with the operator on 2026-10-28. The kit attached to the second project's wiki tools page was built from 9277f44 and lacks the toolkit work-package update-text command, the task set-title command, the estimate commands and the Apache-2.0 kit notice. Build a fresh kit for that project, check it for private names, endpoints, settings files and bindings, upload it and its checksum as wiki attachments with a dry run first, and update the page text if it names the kit file or lists its commands.

elements.subject: Record a task's actual window as its planned dates on acceptance

description.raw: Agreed with the operator on 2026-10-28. replan next lists 31 accepted tasks whose planned window is still in the future, because acceptance records the status but leaves the planned dates; validation warns accepted_task_planned_after_status_date and asks for a scenario per task. Add replan task record-actual-window --task <id> that derives the actual start and finish the way replan report estimates does (status audit records first, then consumption actuals, the source reported), writes them as the planned dates with an audit record and evidence, dry run by default, and refuses a task that is not accepted or has no actual dates. scripts/accept-task.sh runs it after acceptance and pushes the dates to OpenProject; the validation warning names the new command. The sealed baselines keep the original planned dates.

elements.subject: Record the actual windows of the accepted self-dogfood tasks

description.raw: Agreed with the operator on 2026-10-28. Run replan task record-actual-window on every accepted task of examples/replan-self whose planned window differs from its actual window (31 tasks on 2026-10-28), review the derived dates and their sources, push the dates to OpenProject with the reviewed date helper and check that OpenProject did not move any of them onto another working day (finding C-18). Afterwards replan validate has no accepted_task_planned_after_status_date warning and replan next no record-actual-window item.

elements.subject: Version the project file format

description.raw: Agreed with the operator on 2026-10-28, from the public roadmap: outside users will keep data in RePlan files, so the format needs a version before the repository is published. Add a format version to the project manifest, write it in every example and in new projects, load a project without one as the first version with a warning, refuse a newer version than the binary knows with a clear error and exit code, and add replan project migrate (dry run by default) that upgrades a project to the current version, with nothing to change yet. Document the version rule and the migration promise in storage-layout and cli.

elements.subject: Add replan version and a local release build

description.raw: Agreed with the operator on 2026-10-28, from the public roadmap. Add replan version (text and JSON: version, commit, build date, Go version, project format version), set at build time and falling back to the module build info for go install. Add scripts/build-release.sh that builds linux, macOS and Windows binaries for amd64 and arm64 from a clean tagged tree, packs each with LICENSE, NOTICE and README, and writes SHA256SUMS; CI is paused, so the release build runs locally. Document the release steps and the go install path in a release runbook.

elements.subject: Publish the public repository

description.raw: Agreed with the operator on 2026-10-28. Follow docs/dev/public-repository-cut.md: rerun the sanitized cut on the publication day, rename the current repository to its history name, create the public repository under the same owner with one first commit, switch this checkout in place, enable private vulnerability reporting and check the README links on GitHub. Publishing and creating repositories is the operator's step; the agent prepares the cut and checks it.

elements.subject: Publish the first tagged release

description.raw: Agreed with the operator on 2026-10-28. Tag v0.1.0 on the public repository, build the archives with scripts/build-release.sh, check the checksums and that each binary reports the tag in replan version, and publish a GitHub release with the archives and short notes that say the project is alpha. Creating the tag and the release is the operator's step.

elements.subject: Design how estimate accuracy feeds back into planning

description.raw: Agreed with the operator on 2026-10-28, from the public roadmap. The estimate report shows actual over baseline per resource (0.26 for the agents on the 2026-10-15 baseline). Design how that becomes a calibration: per resource and, if the data allows, per task type or tag; a minimum sample and the treatment of tasks booked by judgement; whether calibration only suggests (proposals that scale open demands, accepted by a person) or also informs new estimates; how a calibration is recorded, sealed and audited; and what replan report estimates and replan next show. The operator approves the design before implementation.

elements.subject: Implement estimate calibration

description.raw: Implement the approved estimate calibration design (task.self.design-estimate-calibration) with tests on a fixture, documentation in cli and report-behavior, and a first run on examples/replan-self whose calibration scenario the operator reviews. Minimum sample 8 tasks, the six judged tasks of 15-16 October excluded, one quarter-unit rounding rule.

elements.subject: Choose and design a second task tracker adapter

description.raw: Agreed with the operator on 2026-10-28, from the public roadmap: a second tracker proves the model is not shaped around OpenProject. Compare candidates (GitHub Issues with sub-issues and issue dependencies, GitLab, Plane), recommend one, and design the read-only mapping to the canonical model: identity and source refs, status, dates, assignees, relations, estimates and time, sidecars for what the tracker lacks, and staged import with manual accept as for OpenProject. The operator chooses the tracker and approves the design.

elements.subject: Import GitHub Issues from an exported file

description.raw: Implement the approved second tracker design (task.self.design-second-tracker-adapter) for GitHub Issues from file input first: the mapper with a label-based in-progress status, staged snapshot and candidates, replan import accept for each candidate type, sanitized fixtures and tests, and documentation, without network access.

elements.subject: Import GitHub Issues over the API

description.raw: Add live GitHub API input for the GitHub Issues adapter: token from an environment variable, pagination, rate limits, timeouts and retries for reads, issue dependencies and sub-issues, a profile in the project manifest, and a check against a separate disposable test repository, not the RePlan public repository. Read-only; write-back is out of scope.

elements.subject: Decide which views a small web view needs

description.raw: Agreed with the operator on 2026-10-28, from the public roadmap. Review which dashboard pages and CLI reports the operator and the agents actually used during the dogfood cycle, and design a small local web view only for those: candidates are the weekly load heatmap, scenario comparison and proposal review with accept and reject behind the same approval rules as the CLI. Say what it reads, how it is served locally, how it writes nothing without approval, and what stays in the static dashboard. The operator approves the scope before implementation.

elements.subject: Add the workload, scenario, proposal and estimate pages to the static dashboard

description.raw: Implement the approved local web view decision (task.self.design-local-web-view): add workload.html, scenarios.html, proposals.html and estimates.html to the static dashboard, read-only and working from disk, with HTML goldens like the existing pages, the raw JSON each page reads, and the smoke generating them from a temporary copy of examples/replan-self. No served application and no OpenProject plugin page in this task.

elements.subject: Keep dates on non-working days in OpenProject

description.raw: Found on 2026-10-28 while dry-running replan task record-actual-window over the accepted self-dogfood tasks: 27 of the 97 windows to record start or finish on a Saturday or Sunday, because work was done then. OpenProject's working-day calendar moves such dates to the next working day (finding C-18), so after the push those work packages would show other dates than RePlan and stay in date drift. Check on the throwaway OpenProject whether setting the work package's ignoreNonWorkingDays (working days only off) keeps a weekend date, and if so make the toolkit update-dates, push-openproject-date-drift.sh and the accept-task date step set it when a pushed date falls on a non-working day, with tests and a live check on one work package; otherwise record the platform limit and make the drift checks treat a date moved by the calendar as aligned with a stated reason.

elements.subject: Keep the self OpenProject sample in step with accepted dates

description.raw: Since accept-task records the actual window and pushes it to OpenProject (task.self.record-actual-task-window), every acceptance moves the task's planned dates. The committed sanitized OpenProject sample (examples/imports/openproject/replan-self.work-packages.sample.json) keeps the old dates, so the smoke's date-push review count grows by one per accepted task and the smoke fails until the sample is edited by hand. Found on 2026-10-29 when eight acceptances moved the count from 25 to 33. Wanted: the documented sample update path (REPLAN_UPDATE_GOLDEN=1 for TestSelfOpenProjectSampleAgreesWithCanonicalTasks, or a helper beside it) also refreshes startDate and dueDate of entries whose task is accepted and has a recorded actual window, and their subject after a rename, without touching the deliberate drift entries the smoke relies on; the smoke's count stops depending on how many tasks were accepted; the procedure in the agent kit and backlog convention says when to run it.

elements.subject: Keep OpenProject successors manually scheduled after relations

description.raw: Found on 2026-10-29 while recording the actual windows of the accepted tasks: eight of 165 self-dogfood work packages were automatically scheduled in OpenProject (scheduleManually false), the seven created on 2026-10-28 and one older accepted task. OpenProject moved them when their predecessors' dates changed: the six open roadmap tasks to the day after their predecessors (two to eleven working days earlier than RePlan's dates) when accept-task pushed the designs' actual windows, and the accepted task one day earlier when the backfill moved its predecessor to a Sunday. The date helpers already set scheduleManually true; the likely cause is that creating a follows relation with apply-openproject-relations.sh switches the successor to automatic scheduling, and nothing switches it back. The dates were restored with push-openproject-date-drift.sh and work-package update-dates. Wanted: confirm the cause on the throwaway runtime; keep or restore manual scheduling of a bound successor when a relation is created, without changing its dates, through the reviewed relation helper with its dry run and apply gate; report a bound work package that is automatically scheduled as a drift warning code in check-openproject-drift.sh, and give date drift a warning code too so a soft date drift is not only a count; tests and the helper docs.

elements.subject: Report unknown build details plainly in replan version

description.raw: Found on 2026-10-29 after publishing v0.1.0: a binary installed with go install github.com/kogriv/replan/cmd/replan@v0.1.0 (or @latest) through the public module proxy prints replan v0.1.0 (dev, dev, go1.24.1 linux/amd64), and replan version --format json reports commit dev and build_date dev, because module downloads carry no VCS stamp. The release archives are not affected. Wanted: when the version is a module version but the commit or the build date is unknown, the text line leaves the unknown parts out (for example replan v0.1.0 (go1.24.1 linux/amd64)) and the JSON says unknown in a documented way instead of dev, with dev kept for a plain local build without a version; tests with a debug.BuildInfo for that case; docs/dev/release-process.md and docs/spec/cli.md say what a go install build reports.

elements.subject: Name shared import candidates source-neutrally

description.raw: Found on 2026-10-29 while checking the live GitHub import: the shared import candidates still carry OpenProject names. A GitHub dependency candidate has from_work_package_id and to_work_package_id, and the Go types are OpenProjectTaskCandidate, OpenProjectResourceCandidate and so on, although import accept and both importers now share them. Renaming the JSON fields would break readers of the existing OpenProject output (helpers, the agent kit, goldens). Wanted: source-neutral Go type names; source-neutral JSON fields for the dependency and resource candidates (for example predecessor_source_id and successor_source_id) added beside the old ones, with the old OpenProject-named fields kept for OpenProject snapshots and documented as deprecated; GitHub snapshots use only the neutral names; the helpers that read the old fields keep working; docs/spec/cli.md and the GitHub document spec updated; goldens through the documented path.

elements.subject: Publish release v0.2.0

description.raw: Agreed with the operator on 2026-10-29: after the source-neutral import candidates, publish v0.2.0 with estimate calibration, the GitHub Issues import from a file and over the API, the workload, scenario, proposal and estimate dashboard pages, the OpenProject successor scheduling fix and the replan version fix. Follow docs/dev/release-process.md: release commit with CI green, annotated tag on GitHub and GitLab, archives with scripts/build-release.sh, checksums, a reproducibility rebuild, binary version check, GitHub release with notes saying the project is alpha, and go install through the module proxy.

elements.subject: Refresh the second project's agent kit to v0.2.0

description.raw: Agreed with the operator on 2026-10-29: refresh the second project's agent kit to release v0.2.0, as task.self.refresh-second-project-agent-kit did for the 28 October kit. Build the kit for that project with build-agent-kit.sh, check it offline and on a throwaway OpenProject, scan it for private details, upload the archive and its checksum to the tools wiki page with a dry run first, verify the download against the checksum, and update the page text: the new kit rows and what changed since the 28 October kit (the version command, relation apply restoring manual scheduling, the drift check's new warning codes, the GitHub import, estimate calibration and the dashboard pages). Deleting older kit attachments is the operator's decision.

elements.subject: Update the roadmap after release v0.2.0

description.raw: Agreed with the operator on 2026-10-30: ROADMAP.md still lists estimate calibration, the GitHub Issues import and the dashboard pages under Next although release v0.2.0 shipped them. Move them to Works today, keep the stable file format under Next with its condition, and add the next directions agreed in chat: onboarding for a first project of one's own, estimate calibration by size band, GitHub Projects fields in the live import, and release builds in GitHub Actions. Each direction still becomes a self plan task before work starts.

elements.subject: Design onboarding for a first project of one's own

description.raw: Agreed with the operator on 2026-10-30 as the next work after the roadmap update: today a new user can only start a project of their own by writing the YAML files by hand; there is no replan init, no command to add resources or capacities, and no short guide from an empty directory to a first workload report. Write a design note for first-project onboarding: what replan init creates, which resource and capacity commands are needed, how a first task with a demand is added, what the quickstart guide covers and what stays out of scope. Bring the design to the operator for decisions before any implementation task is planned.
